slides.title: Laval is an island. 5 riverside spots to know.
slides.sub: From Île Bigras to Laval-sur-le-Lac, what each one is like.

photo.credit: Photo: Maxime Laterreur, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

slides.title: Île Bigras: an island with a REM stop

photo.credit: Photo: 이동아, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

slides.body: Part of Îles-Laval, with its own REM station. About **27 minutes** to Central Station at full service.

slides.title: Vieux-Saint-Vincent-de-Paul

photo.credit: Photo: Jeangagnon, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

slides.body: Settled in **1740**, near the Rivière des Prairies. A heritage main street, terraces and a church from **1853**.

slides.title: Auteuil: quiet Mille Îles shoreline
slides.body: On Laval's north side: a former summer-cottage area by the river, with small parks along the water.
slides.source: Per Ville de Laval heritage study, 2020

slides.title: Laval-sur-le-Lac: where 3 waters meet
slides.body: Low-density streets, big lots and no sidewalks. Created as its own town in **1915**.
slides.source: Per Ville de Laval heritage study, 2020

slides.title: Love the water? Check the map first
slides.body: Look up any riverside address before you offer. Then ask your insurer what flood coverage would cost.

slides.title: Moving to Laval? Let's find your spot.
slides.tagline: Let's break this down together. No rush.
